title: A short note on agent sandboxing
body: A sandbox is an execution environment that bounds the side effects available to an agent. It does not lower the probability of a bad action; it caps the cost. Default-deny is the guiding principle: grant capabilities explicitly.

title: Guardrails in one paragraph
body: Guardrails decide which proposed actions execute at all. An action policy returns allow, confirm, or deny per tool call, enforced in code the model cannot rewrite. A denied call is returned as an error the agent can react to.

title: Why layers
body: No single layer suffices. Model rules, guardrails, sandbox isolation and human oversight fail independently, so each catches what the one above let through.
